findings.title: Unguarded property access crashes create() when no destination calendar exists
findings.body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` comes from `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` destructuring, so it is `undefined` when the array is empty. The next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. For a Google Meet location with no destination calendar (for example a booking where the organizer has no destinationCalendar row), this throws a TypeError and the booking creation fails. It should be `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback lookup compares against the wrong value and always resolves to undefined
findings.body: In the fallback branch (externalCalendarId falsy), the code does `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. Since externalCalendarId is falsy here, the comparison can never match a real externalId, so the result is always undefined. The same broken expression is at line 317 in deleteEvent. Consequences: updateEvent sends `calendarId: undefined`, and deleteEvent falls back to "primary", so events stored on a non-primary calendar are not updated or deleted. The lookup should match on credentialId, as createEvent does.

findings.title: Lark createEvent always uses the first destination calendar, so multi-host collective events are not created per host
findings.body: Lark's createEvent, createAttendees, updateEvent and deleteEvent all take `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar` and ignore which credential is calling. CalendarManager calls each credential's createEvent with the full destination array. In a collective event with two hosts, every host's Lark credential therefore writes to host #1's calendar, and host #2's calendar gets no event. The same pattern applies to Office365 (createEvent, line 73 of that file) and CalDAV (createEvent filter in packages/lib/CalendarService.ts). The PR's stated goal of letting each host receive the event is not met for these integrations.

findings.title: The destination externalId is attached to the result but never passed to the calendar services
findings.body: createEvent now receives `externalId` and calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`, dropping the externalId. Only the Google service uses the credential to pick a calendar. Other services read event.destinationCalendar[0] or filter by it, so the per-destination externalId is lost. EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents (line 370) passes `destination.externalId` into createEvent, which is then discarded, so each destination entry results in the same write. The result's `externalId` field is also set from an argument that does nothing for these integrations, so the references stored for the booking will not match the calendars actually written to.

findings.title: Team destination calendars are silently dropped when the organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither eventType nor organizer has a destination calendar. The following line does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`, which is a no-op on null. For a collective event where the organizer has no destination but other hosts do, the other hosts' calendars are never used, which is the exact scenario this PR is meant to fix. The array should be initialised rather than optionally pushed to.

findings.title: Team destination calendars can be duplicated and are collected inside a parallel map
findings.body: teamDestinationCalendars is pushed inside `users.slice(1).map(async ...)`. The push happens before the await in each callback, so ordering is nondeterministic. Also, if multiple hosts share a destination calendar or an existing entry is already in evt.destinationCalendar, duplicates are not removed, so createAllCalendarEvents will write the same event more than once. Collecting the calendars synchronously after the users list is built, then de-duplicating by id, would avoid both problems.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation deletes the same events once per calendar reference
findings.body: The loop now iterates over every calendar reference. Inside the recurring branch, for each reference it maps over all user calendar credentials and deletes every updated booking's calendar event again. With two calendar references (the multi-host case this PR enables), each booking's event is deleted twice or more, and the duplicate deleteEvent calls push extra promises into apiDeletes. The recurring deletion should run once, outside the per-reference loop.

findings.title: Inverted condition on slug and requestedSlug, unrelated to the PR
findings.body: The original code was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`. The new code is `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which includes slug when billing is enabled and omits it when disabled. This is a logic inversion, and the same inversion applies to `requestedSlug` on the following line. It changes organization creation behaviour for every installation and is not mentioned in the PR description.

findings.title: Office365 createEvent ignores the credential and writes every destination to the first calendar
findings.body: createEvent reads `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and uses that calendar's externalId for the URL. With multiple destinations, each per-destination createEvent call writes an event to the first calendar rather than the one belonging to its credential. This creates duplicate events on one account and none on the others.

findings.title: No tests added for the multi-host collective behaviour being fixed
findings.body: The PR adds a new multi-destination code path in EventManager, CalendarManager and the booking handlers, but the checklist says no tests were added and the testing section relies on manual Loom recordings. Given how many call sites changed from a single destination to an array, unit tests for EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents and updateAllCalendarEvents with multiple destinations would be needed to catch the regressions above.
